files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS barn south and east elevations.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
The foundation is stone, and the barn is composed of local timber, walnut framing with peg connections; the roof is a metal standing seam installed in the late 1950s.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS barn west elevation.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
There is a wood framed, corrugated metal clad garage/shed structure attached to the west portion of the barn.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS barn north and east elevations.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
 On the north façade, there are two sets of Dutch doors and one pair of barn doors.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS barn southwest corner.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
Located approximately 170’ northeast of the farmhouse, the barn is composed of a rectangular volume running lengthwise east to west, approximately 30’x35’ rising two stories topped by a gable roof, with a one-story shed-roof extension on the west extending approximately 20 additional feet.
